bibliographic.title: Observation of spin-conserving two-spinon continuum in the S=1/2 antiferromagnetic chain system Sr2CuO3 using Cu K-edge resonant inelastic x-ray scattering

affiliations.text: Synchrotron Radiation Research Center, National Institutes for Quantum Science and Technology, Hyogo 679-5148, Japan
Department of Applied Physics, Tohoku University, Sendai 980-8579, Japan

bibliographic.abstract: We report a Cu K-edge resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) study of spin excitations in the S=1/2 antiferromagnetic chain system Sr2CuO3. The spectral weight observed below the chargetransfer gap appears in two-spinon continuum, indicating the fractionalization of a spin-conserving (ΔS = 0) magnetic excitation into two-spinon states. The intensity of these excitations reaches a maximum near the midpoint between the center and the boundary of the Brillouin zone, and decreases toward the zone boundary; this behavior contrasts with that of the spin-flip (ΔS = 1) excitations typically observed via inelastic neutron scattering or Cu L3-edge RIXS. The momentum dependence of the intensity is described by the spin-exchange dynamical structure factor. A phenomenological analysis of the symmetry between the polarization and the d orbital explains the resonance condition for the two-spinon excitations.

samples.sample_description: Single crystal grown using the traveling-solvent floating-zone technique.

datasets.dataset_description: Measured in total fluorescence mode to determine incident photon energies.
Measurement of spin excitations in the two-spinon continuum with varying incident photon energy and polarization.
